title.value: Reward Propagation Using Graph Convolutional Networks
title.justification: The title 'Reward Propagation Using Graph Convolutional Networks' is the exact title mentioned in the citation and throughout the paper, indicating the focus on using Graph Convolutional Networks for reward propagation in reinforcement learning.
title.quote: Reward Propagation Using Graph Convolutional Networks

analysis.description: This paper introduces a novel framework for learning potential functions within reinforcement learning by leveraging Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs). The approach aims to improve the learning process by utilizing GCNs to propagate messages from rewarding states, ultimately providing potential functions for reward shaping. The framework is tested empirically across various environments, including tabular domains, vision-based navigation tasks, Atari games, and MuJoCo continuous control tasks, demonstrating significant improvements compared to traditional methods.

type.justification: The paper presents empirical results from experiments conducted on various environments, such as the MiniWorld environment, Atari 2600 benchmark, and MuJoCo environments, showing the practical application and effectiveness of their proposed method.
type.quote: We first evaluate our approach in tabular domains where we achieve similar performance compared to potential based reward shaping built on the forward-backward algorithm. Unlike hand-engineered potential functions, our method scales naturally to more complex environments; we illustrate this on navigation-based vision tasks from the MiniWorld environment, on a variety of games from the Atari 2600 benchmark and on a set of continuous control environments based on MuJoCo.

name.justification: The paper focuses on enhancing the reinforcement learning process by learning potential functions through reward shaping using GCNs, which is a central concern in the field of reinforcement learning.
name.quote: In particular, we are interested in formulating the RL problem as a directed graph whose structure is analogous to hidden Markov models.

name.justification: The use of Graph Convolutional Networks, a type of Graph Neural Network, is a core component of the proposed method, used for message passing and reward propagation in reinforcement learning.
name.quote: We use Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) to propagate information about the rewards in an environment through the message passing mechanism defined by the GCN’s structural bias and loss function.

name.justification: The focus on potential-based reward shaping to enhance the learning process is central to the proposed method, distinguishing it as a subfield within reinforcement learning explored in this paper.
name.quote: Our approach can be understood as an attempt to accelerate learning by emphasizing information about rewarding states through potential functions with the guarantee of preserving the optimal policy.

is_executed.quote: Our approach shows significant improvements over the classic actor-critic algorithm, which suggests that our method is able to provide the agent with valuable information to accelerate learning.
